newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MEP slams extension of transit regime to E Europe.
newsitem.headline: MEP slams extension of transit regime to E Europe.

text.p: Extending the European Union's fraud-ridden transit regime to Central and East European states could be a disaster unless the EU reforms the existing system first, a British Socialist MEP warned on Tuesday.
"The system is sufficiently bad that the European Parliament chose to...set up a committee of inquiry. It shouldn't be further extended until reform has taken place," MEP John Tomlinson told Reuters.

Tomlinson, who chairs the European Parliament's committee of inquiry into customs fraud in the transit system, said the EU had been ill-advised to open up the system on July 1, 1996 to the so-called Visegrad countries of Poland, Hungary, and the Czech and Slovak Republics.
"It seems to us to be a slightly bizarre way of dealing with things, that when you've got a system that is not working for 15 (countries) you enlarge it," he said.

The MEP said he would challenge Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti during the parliament's plenary session in Brussels on Thursday over the European Commission's plans for possibly opening up the regime to other countries seeking EU membership.

On behalf of the Socialist group, Tomlinson will urge the Commission not to extend the system to any other country with which the EU has negotiated an Association Agreement until reforms to it are proving effective in reducing fraud.

The Commission and the European Court of Auditors estimate some 200 million Ecus are lost from the EU budget every year as a result of fraud against the system, notably relating to cigarettes, spirits and other goods subject to high duty rates.
The parliament's commission of inquiry is due to recommend in December a series of improvements to the transit regime.

These are likely to include calls for swifter and more accurate transfer of information on goods in transit through the EU and a system for validating goods leaving EU territory which is less easy to forge, Tomlinson said.
